title: An explanation of the hierarchy between the gravitational and particle mass scales

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 9 (proposed by Matt Strassler): what physics explains the enormous disparity between the gravitational scale and the typical mass scale of the elementary particles? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

page.title: Resolution of the electroweak hierarchy problem
page.definition: An experimentally supported physical explanation of why the electroweak scale, the Higgs field's value in the vacuum, is about 10^17 times smaller than the Planck scale, formed from Newton's gravitational constant, the speed of light and Planck's constant.

goal.need: The electroweak scale is v ≈ 246 GeV; the unreduced Planck energy is E_P = 1.220890(14) × 10^19 GeV. Their calculated ratio is about 2.0 × 10^-17. The Standard Model fits its Higgs mass parameter to observations. Additional heavy particles coupled to the Higgs can generate corrections proportional to their squared masses, making the origin of the separation a question about the underlying physics.

figures.caption: The separation between electroweak and gravitational scales
figures.note: Using ħ = c = 1, v is calculated from CODATA's Fermi constant through v = (√2 G_F)^−1/2. The ratio is calculated. Parentheses give one standard uncertainty in the final digits.

completion.title: A validated physical mechanism quantitatively accounts for the electroweak–Planck hierarchy.
completion.criterion: A peer-reviewed physical explanation accounts for v/E_P ≈ 2.0 × 10^-17, using the unreduced Planck scale and units ħ = c = 1. The separation follows from specified dynamics, symmetry or selection conditions, with its dependence on free parameters and quantum corrections explicit. Independent measurements corroborate predictions that identify the proposed mechanism.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no model-independent completion test was found in the sources searched.
completion.basis: Strings 2000, P5 2023, NASEM 2025, PDG's Higgs review and Peskin's hierarchy review were searched for a solution criterion, a numerical fine-tuning cutoff and a validation protocol. None supplied a model-independent completion test. This fallback combines the stated demand for an explanation of the scale separation with experimental identification of its mechanism.

milestones.title: A Higgs-boson candidate is observed with at least 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: A boson compatible with the Higgs hypothesis is observed at ≥5σ significance. Papers submitted on 31 July 2012 reported 5.9σ for ATLAS and 5.0σ local significance for CMS. ATLAS used approximately 4.8 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.8 fb^-1 at 8 TeV; CMS used up to 5.1 fb^-1 and 5.3 fb^-1, respectively. These peer-reviewed results establish the experimental starting point.

milestones.title: A proposed hierarchy mechanism's predicted new effect is observed with at least 5σ significance.
milestones.criterion: A proposed hierarchy explanation's new-particle signal or distinguishing effect rejects the known-process hypothesis at ≥5σ; an upward fluctuation corresponds to p ≤ 2.87 × 10^-7. Search-range effects and systematic uncertainties enter the assessment. A CMS preliminary report dated 6 July 2026 instead constrained Higgs compositeness using 207 fb^-1 at 13 and 13.6 TeV: its one-parameter fit gave −2.1 × 10^-4 < W < 1.6 × 10^-4 at 95% confidence, with Y fixed to zero. W and Y describe corrections to electroweak gauge-boson propagation. This result is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention described by the Particle Data Group, Statistics, section 40.3.2; applied here to a candidate hierarchy mechanism's signal.
milestones.threshold_quote:
a discovery
is Z = 5, i.e., a 5σ effect

milestones.title: Measurements satisfy a proposed hierarchy mechanism's distinguishing parameter relations.
milestones.criterion: Independent measurements satisfy the proposed mechanism's published distinguishing relations within stated experimental and theoretical uncertainties, with enough precision to constrain those relations. For weakly coupled partner models, relevant tests include mass–coupling sum rules and relative coupling signs. The study published on 22 May 2019 used simulated 100 TeV proton collisions with an assumed 30 ab^-1 dataset; it did not observe partner particles. Explaining the full electroweak–Planck separation remains the completion test.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of PDG, P5, NASEM and hierarchy reviews found no mechanism-independent validation threshold. Csáki and colleagues supply a specific sum-rule test for weakly coupled partner explanations, not a universal criterion.

not_found: No model-independent completion criterion or numerical fine-tuning acceptance threshold was found in the committee reports and hierarchy reviews searched.
No common experimental precision or universal sequence of milestones was found for the competing hierarchy explanations.
